device.name: Gerbing / GYDE ThermoGauge Heated Clothing Controller
device.notes:
BLE controller for Gerbing heated clothing. Supports dual-channel heat control (2 independent zones) and dual temperature sensor inputs depending on hardware variant. Product names "coreheat7" (7.4V) and "coreheat12" (12V) — voltage detected from advertised name. Xamarin.Forms Android app.
UUID EXTRACTION: All 10 UUIDs recovered from ThermoGauge.Core.dll .NET assembly via IL disassembly. UUIDs are plain string literals in the #US heap (UTF-16LE), not binary Guid structs. Earlier attempts with `strings` (ASCII) and blob scanning failed because the heap is UTF-16LE — `strings -e l` finds them instantly.
HEAT WRITE FORMAT: 1 byte, (byte)float value, 0-100 percent.
  Channel A: HeatChar1 (90759319-…)
  Channel B: HeatChar2 (80c37f00-…)
  Heat >100: untested, app does not clamp — treat as unsafe.

TEMP READ FORMAT: 1 byte, unsigned. Display: ceil((raw/2+85)/5)*5.
  Units: inferred °F (raw=0→85, raw=142≈156, raw=255≈215).
  TempControl mode active when 60 <= raw < 142 (~115-155°F) AND
  heat outputs > 0 (Model::get_IsTempControl).

BATTERY: 1 byte, 0-100%, standard SIG Battery Level (0x2A19).
DEVICE TYPE: 1 byte, high nibble = heat outputs, low nibble = temp
  inputs. e.g., 0x21 = 2 outputs, 1 input. Under Device Info
  (0x180A) as custom characteristic 0313fb4e-… (not standard DIS).

SCAN FILTER: name Contains("Gerbing") || Contains("Gyde").
  Not a prefix match — substring anywhere in advertised name.
  Auto-reconnect on device.ID match. The app scans NAME-ONLY —
  it never filters by service UUID, so the advertisement contents
  are unknown from the binary and identification.service_uuids /
  discovery.ble.service_uuids are UNVERIFIABLE for Thermogauge
  hardware. The sibling Snooz device advertises the HEAT service
  729f0608-… (not the temp service), so scanning by ab06bd90-…
  may well miss real devices — scan by name.

POLL LOOP: the app polls characteristics round-robin
  (GetNextCharacteristicToPoll cycles channel index
  1..NumDeviceOutputs) in addition to registering ValueUpdated —
  device-side notify vs poll-only is unconfirmed.

TOKEN-AUTH SURFACE: the shared OEM module natively supports a
  SET_TOKEN command (command id 6, per pysnooz's Snooz command
  table) that the Thermogauge app never exercises. On Snooz, an
  8-byte pairing token rides in the BLE manufacturer data
  (pysnooz advertisement parsing). Whether Thermogauge firmware
  implements or requires token auth is unknown — no auth was
  needed in the app.

BATTERY SAVER: level <=20% triggers heat clamp to max 20 (7.4V only,
  12V exempt). IL set_BatteryLevel: `ldc.i4.s 20; bgt.s end` — the
  equality case clamps too. >=40% deactivates saver.

SHARED OEM MODULE: the Snooz white-noise machine ships the identical
  custom service 729f0608-… with the same chars 90759319-… (write)
  and 80c37f00-… (read/notify) — live-hardware cross-confirmation of
  this UUID family (HA core snooz integration; pysnooz 0.8.6 writes
  [command_id, …data] frames). Frame semantics are per-product
  firmware (Snooz: 2-byte commands; Thermogauge: raw 1-byte level) —
  do NOT port Snooz command tables to Gerbing hardware.

CONFIDENCE: HIGH for all UUIDs and data formats — every value backed by ldstr→stfld IL pairs (UUIDs) or IL bytecode ops (formats). Characteristic *usage* is provable statically (heat chars written + read back; temp/battery read); the advertised property bits are per-product firmware — the Snooz GATT dump shows the same UUIDs with different bits (90759319 write-only, 80c37f00 read+notify), so the properties below list proven usage and notify needs a Thermogauge GATT dump. Remaining unknowns: actual temp units (inferred °F), notify support vs poll-only, firmware heat clamping above 100.

credentials.notes: BLE GATT. No auth or pairing in app source.

factory_reset.effect: Unknown. No factory reset procedure found in app source.

methods.description: Scan for BLE advertisements with name containing "Gerbing" or "Gyde". Connect, discover services, read DeviceType to determine channel counts. Write 1-byte heat levels to HeatChar1/2. Read TempChar1/2 for temperature feedback. Read Battery Level (0x2A19) for battery percentage.

steps.action: Scan for BLE advertisements with name containing Gerbing or Gyde.
Read DeviceType (0313fb4e-…) to determine channel count.

setup.notes: No provisioning required. Scan for devices with "Gerbing" or "Gyde" in their name. Connect, discover services, read device type to determine channel count. No pairing or bonding observed in the app source.

variants.notes: 7.4V battery. Subject to battery-saver heat clamp at 20% or below.
12V battery. Exempt from battery-saver heat clamp.

fields.description: High nibble = heat output channels (1-2). Low nibble = temp sensor inputs (1-2). e.g., 0x21 = 2 outputs, 1 input.
fields.name: channels

HeatLevel.description: 1-byte heat level. Write and read use same format.

fields.description: Single byte, (byte)float_value, 0-100. Values >100 are not clamped by the app — firmware behavior untested.
fields.name: heat_percent

fields.description: Unsigned byte 0-255. TempControl valid when 60 <= raw < 142. Display formula: ceil((raw/2+85)/5)*5 (inferred °F).
fields.name: temp_raw

characteristics.name: Device Type
characteristics.notes: Custom characteristic under standard DIS. 1 byte: high nibble = number of heat output channels, low nibble = number of temperature sensor inputs. e.g., 0x21 = 2 outputs, 1 input. Drives single/ dual-channel UI. Nibbles A-F silently fail to parse (app uses int.TryParse per character from X2 format).

format.name: temp_raw
format.notes: Linear decode is value = raw * 0.5 + 85; on top of that the vendor app rounds UP to the next multiple of 5 for display (ceil(value/5)*5). Units are inferred °F, not confirmed (raw=0 -> 85, raw=142 ≈ 156, raw=255 -> 212.5 shown as 215). TempControl mode is active while 60 <= raw < 142 and heat outputs are above 0.

characteristics.name: Temperature Channel 1
characteristics.notes: 1 unsigned byte. Display: ceil((raw/2+85)/5)*5, inferred °F. Valid control range: 60 <= raw < 142 (~115-155°F). Read usage proven statically; the app also registers ValueUpdated, so notify is likely — but property bits are per-product firmware (see device notes) and need a Thermogauge GATT dump to confirm.

format.name: temp_raw
format.notes: Same decode and inferred-°F caveat as Channel 1.

characteristics.name: Temperature Channel 2
characteristics.notes: Same format as Channel 1. Only active on dual-input devices. Same property-bits caveat as Channel 1.

services.name: Temperature Service
services.notes: Custom service. Two temperature sensor channels. UUID family uses vendor base cc16-11e4-8830-0800200c9a66 (version-1 timestamp ~2014).

characteristics.name: Battery Level
characteristics.notes: Standard SIG Battery Level. 1 unsigned byte, 0-100%. Read usage proven statically; notify unconfirmed (property bits are per-product firmware — see device notes).

format.name: heat_percent
format.notes: 0-100; the app does not clamp above 100 and firmware behavior there is untested — treat >100 as unsafe.

characteristics.name: Heat Channel 1
characteristics.notes: 1 byte: (byte)heat_level where heat_level is a float 0-100. Write: new byte[1] { (byte)value }. Same byte format for read. Labels: <=25=LO, <=50=MED, <=75=HI, >75=EXTRM. Write + read-back usage proven statically; notify unconfirmed — on the sibling Snooz device this exact UUID is write-only (property bits are per-product firmware, see device notes).

characteristics.name: Heat Channel 2
characteristics.notes: Same format as Channel 1. Only active on dual-output devices. Same property-bits caveat as Channel 1 (on Snooz this UUID is read+notify — per-product firmware).

services.name: Heat Control Service
services.notes: Custom service. Two independent heat channels. UUIDs are mutually unrelated (not suffixes of a common base) — HeatChar1, HeatChar2, and the service itself are three different UUIDs.
